cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Tell Me Why
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal the motive behind a choice by offering small pieces of your own truth as bait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I once hid an invitation because I felt left out. Why hide mine? Please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I nearly skipped your birthday when you invited Leah. Is this about being alone?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's about you liking her more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I counted your photos with her after that party. Did you hide mine to make me choose you?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1, A3 and A5 each offer personal jealousy truth before a motive question, but A3 authority adjustment is not enacted in the relationship.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 fear of being left develops through B4 preferring Leah; A5 photos are another stated personal truth, not invented by the reader.

relationship.evidence: B2 gives a surface motive and B4 corrects the alone interpretation with rivalry.

heightening.evidence: B4 liking her more prompts A5 a more embarrassing parallel and a choosing-me motive test.

specificity.evidence: A1 hidden invitation and A3 Leah birthday establish the conflict; A5 mine after photos should name invitation to avoid referent drift.

brevityWit.evidence: A1 voluntary please and A3 rank clause are detached; A5 could name the object directly.
